title: Payload Autopsy Timeline & Retry Hypotheses Canvas
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Design a composable debugging lane inside Redwood Console that surfaces a chronological ‘autopsy’ of failed requests, overlays retry attempts and circuit-breaker events, and lets operators pin hypotheses about root cause. This canvas focuses on blending temporal tracing (request->retry->fallback) with payload diffs and error taxonomy filtering so engineers can rapidly validate whether a failure is systemic, client-side, or model-related. The prototype should be usable as a live inspection tool for requests in the last 30 days and as a snapshot for archived incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Canvas exposes an ordered timeline of request attempts including initial, retries, and fallback variants with per-step metadata (latency, model, quantization profile, node region)
Payload diff viewer shows side-by-side normalized inputs (prompt + metadata) and outputs with ability to toggle tokenized view and KV cache snapshots
Error taxonomy filter allows grouping by error class (network, model-internal, timeout, rate-limit, validation) and persists the filter across timeline scrubbing
Operators can add and save freeform hypotheses tied to a timestamped timeline marker; hypotheses can reference PRs, dashboards, or runbooks
Prototype integrates a mock live stream mode for replaying request sequences and an export button that generates a linkable incident snapshot for Slack/Confluence
Design review sign-off captured from PM (Jared Moreno) and Eng leads (Sasha Petrov) before handoff to frontend
comments: 2025-02-27 Aisha: Kickoff — mapped current console error surfaces to a rough mental model. Decided to prioritize timeline-first flow over list-first to better support triage.
2025-02-28 Marco: Early sketch validated with two SEs; they asked for node-region and model-variant columns in the timeline. Added to ACs.

2025-03-01 PM Jared Moreno: Suggested explicit linkage to rollout policy metadata (canary id, rollout percentage) for cases where a bad rollout could explain spikes. Adding as dependency to ENG rollout telemetry work.
2025-03-03 Sasha Petrov (Eng): Flagged performance concerns for live replay on large payloads; recommended a progressive fetch strategy and server-side diffing. Dev task logged ENG-8921.
2025-03-04 Design critique: Team prefers hypothesis cards that can be attached to timeline markers and optionally converted into a follow-up ticket (PM flow). Prototype updated in Figma.
2025-03-05 Marco: Preparing handoff notes; will include implementation constraints for tokenized view and a fallback static snapshot for archived incidents. Requesting final review by 2025-03-09.
ux_notes: Prefer a condensed header per timeline entry with expandable detail panes to avoid cognitive overload
Color-code error taxonomy and keep a small legend sticky to the canvas
Allow operators to collapse retries into an aggregated node, but keep ability to expand for full sequence
When payload size > 500KB use a truncated view and surface a ‘download full payload’ action
Hypothesis cards should support markdown, links, and a 'promote to ticket' action that pre-fills PM fields
risks: Live replay can be expensive if we naively stream full payloads for long-running incidents. Also potential PII exposure in payload diffs — must pair with redaction policy and include an option to view masked vs unmasked fields.
decisions: Timeline-first: canvas opens to chronological view instead of list view
Server-side diffing for payload normalization to reduce client CPU and bandwidth
Hypotheses are persisted as first-class entities and can be converted to PM tickets
